chunks: About a man who purchased pasture in which he grazes for fifty dirhams, or less or more, and then wanted to admit with him others who would graze with him and take the price from them.
He said: Let him admit with him whomever he wishes for part of what he paid. And if he admits others with him for forty-nine dirhams, so that his sheep graze for one dirham, then there is no harm.

And he does not have the right to sell it for fifty dirhams and graze with them, unless he has done some work in the pasture: dug a well or split a stream, with the approval of the owners of the pasture. Then there is no harm in selling it for more than what he bought it for, because he has done work in it, and therefore it is permissible for him.

key_terms.الثَّمَنَ: the price or fee taken from others
key_terms.بِخَمْسِينَ دِرْهَمًا: for fifty dirhams as the purchase amount
key_terms.بِرِضَا أَصْحَابِ الْمَرْعَى: with the consent of the owners of the pasture
key_terms.حَفَرَ بِئْرًا: dug a well, indicating added labor or improvement
key_terms.شَقَّ نَهَرًا: channeled a stream, indicating enhancement of the land

ai.seo_question: Can a person resell grazing rights for a profit while still using the pasture himself?
ai.summary: This hadith explains a legal ruling concerning shared grazing rights and financial exchange. It permits a person to include others in the use of pasture for part of his cost, but prohibits reselling the same right at full price while retaining benefit for himself unless he has added value through actual work. The ruling emphasizes fairness in transactions and the legitimacy of profit only when accompanied by real contribution.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: about a man who purchased grazing land for fifty dirhams, or more or less, to graze his livestock, and then wanted to allow others to graze with him and charge them a fee.

Imam (as) said: "He may allow others to graze with him for part of what he paid. For example, if he includes others for forty-nine dirhams and his livestock grazes for one dirham, there is no harm in it.

However, he is not allowed to sell the grazing rights for fifty dirhams and graze with them unless he has done some work on the pasture, such as digging a well or channeling a stream with the consent of the pasture owners. In that case, there is no harm in selling it for more than what he purchased it for, because he has added value through his work, making it permissible for him."
